thread:
ana: Heads-up — ScribeCorp reported a large p95/p99 spike after a few GPU OOMs in us-west2. p95 went from ~120ms to ~650ms around 03:20 UTC. They attached traces and say auth requests slow down then time out. Ticket #SC-4821.

sre-bot: alert: [us-west2-gpu-pool] 03:18 UTC multiple OOM events detected (node: gpu-prod-7). See /alerts/SC-4821

jamal: @ana can you paste the tenant id and a sample request id? also grab prom queries for allocator_errors and kv_cache_size.

ana: (sorry typo) ana: tenant=scribe-123, sample req id=01GZQ2Y8. Logs + heap profile uploaded: https://internal.redwood/s/case/SC-4821/files

alex: quick summary of what I'm seeing on the pool: gradual KV cache growth + free-list fragmentation -> repeated allocations fall back to slow path -> allocator retries -> higher token latencies even before full OOM. Immediate mitigations to try:
- reduce per-tenant KV cap to 512MB
- enable allocator slab compaction (experimental) on the pool
- throttle long-running requests (prompt length limit) for that tenant

alex: CLI we used in staging:
```
# reduce tenant KV cap
redwoodctl tenant update --id scribe-123 --kv-max 512MB
# enable compaction on pool
redwoodctl pool update --name us-west2-gpu --allocator-compaction enabled
# route small fraction to fallback pool
redwoodctl route add --from scribe-123 --to us-west2-burst --percent 10
```

maria: applied tenant KV cap 512MB and routed 15% of traffic to us-west2-burst. also lowered default batch size for scribe-123. will monitor.

ana: logs snippet around OOM:
```
[03:18:12] alloc: failed to satisfy 24MB, free-list fragmented, retries=4
[03:18:12] gpu: evicting kv pages for tenant scribe-123
[03:18:15] alloc: aborting request, oom on gpu0
[03:18:18] request 01GZQ2Y8: p99=3.1s, downstream-auth timeout
```

jamal: good. please run these PromQL checks and paste graphs: 
- rate(allocator_retries_total[5m])
- max(kv_cache_bytes{tenant="scribe-123"}) by (instance)
- sum(rate(gpu_oom_events_total[1m])) by (pool)

jamal: initial triage notes: compaction should reduce fragmentation but can spike short-term CPU while compacting. recommend canary with 2% traffic first. also consider lowering tenant cache target and enabling adaptive eviction.

alex: +1 to canary. I'll prepare a rollout: compaction=on for pool, 2% traffic for 30m, watch allocator_retries and p95. If compaction increases 95th for unrelated tenants we roll back.

maria: canary scheduled to start in 8m. dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/runtime/compaction-canary

ana: customer notified: we limited KV cache and routed some traffic; told them we're running a canary for a server-side fix. asked for patience.

jamal: long-term action items captured: allocator tuning RFC, implement compact-on-free heuristics, expose tenant-level backpressure knobs, better per-tenant telemetry.

alex: also proposed short-term mitigations to share with sales if customer wants immediate reliability: reserved Dedicated capacity or higher isolation config.

maria: canary started at 03:30 UTC. initial 10m looks OK: allocator_retries down 40% for scribe-123, p95 trending back toward baseline. will let run 30m then increase to 20% if stable.

ana: thanks all. will keep ticket updated and post final postmortem once we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:
